set_text.text: A unit price is the cost of one unit of a product: the pack price divided by how many units the pack holds. The unit can be an item, a pound or an ounce. Two packs only compare fairly when both are priced on the same unit.
Price against quantity, and nothing about quality. Option A's $1.00 a pound only beats Option B's $1.11 if the product inside is the same grade.
Net weight is not always usable weight
A can's net weight includes the liquid it is packed in. When the account uses only the solids, compare on drained weight instead.
Catch weight cases price by the pound
Meat and cheese often ship catch weight, so every case weighs a little differently. There the price per pound is the real price, and the case price moves each time.
Who uses a unit price calculator
It is built for independent food distributors choosing which pack to stock and quote. Anyone comparing two sizes of the same product should put them on one base first.
